title: {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} template used by too-far-future scenario is undocumented in SKILL.md, and SKILL.md now contradicts itself about that scenario
evidence: Scenario (.claude/skills/form-bug-hunt/scenarios/validation/desired-move-in-date-too-far-future.yaml:23): `  desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}"`. SKILL.md substitution step (line 172) lists only: `- `{MOVE_IN_DATE}` → today + 90 days as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. `date -v+90d +%F`)`. SKILL.md templates section (line 278): `Only the boundary-validation scenarios (`desired-move-in-date-in-past`, `-too-far-future`) pin literal dates on purpose.` A grep for MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR across .claude/skills/form-bug-hunt/ hits only the scenario file (its lines 12 and 23), never SKILL.md.
detail: The bug-hunt runner substitutes only documented templates; SKILL.md defines five and {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} is not one. Left literal, the scenario posts a non-date string, fails on the format branch its own description says is covered elsewhere ("Pins the upper-bound branch of validate_move_in_date"), and silently stops testing its target. Line 278 also falsely claims -too-far-future pins a literal date.
recommended_fix: Document {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} (today + 13 months, YYYY-MM-DD) in SKILL.md step 4 and the templates section, and correct line 278 to say only desired-move-in-date-in-past pins a literal date.
